how: Shanghai Weiqi (Go) Club meets weekly on Sundays at The Press near Hankou Lu; beginners are welcome and the organiser brings a board and teaches the rules.
Shanghai Social Chess Club holds relaxed chess meetups on Tuesday evenings in cafes around Jing'an Temple, open to all levels including beginners.
Shanghai Tai Chi Group runs 60-minute beginner-level taichi classes on Sundays at a hotel in Changning, with a trial fee.
venue: Shanghai Tai Chi Group (Shanghai Anadi Hotel)

how: codebar Shanghai runs free coding workshops open to anyone, hosted at rotating venues such as a bookstore in Huangpu.
Language Exchangers Shanghai (about 3,500 members) hosts Friday evening and Sunday afternoon language exchange socials in Xuhui and Changning bars and cafes; a ticket includes a drink.
venue: Language Exchangers Shanghai (Tims Coffee Greenland Wonderful City / Koala Bar)

how: The Inkwell, a writing group founded in 2015, runs free fiction, nonfiction and poetry workshops and open writing sessions at cafes and bars in central Shanghai; no experience required.
The Inkwell holds a free Reading Group every other Monday at Garden Books on Changle Lu.
Shanghai Mahjong Workshop teaches internationals Chinese mahjong in simple English on Sunday afternoons at Happy Mahjong Club on Fumin Lu; described as beginner-friendly.
KL Climbing Park in Libo 1987 has indoor walls of 16 m, 20 m and up to 34 m with auto-belay routes; no natural big walls nearby.
The Shanghai Museum at People's Square holds over 120,000 pieces across eleven permanent galleries of bronzes, ceramics, calligraphy and painting.
Shanghai Science and Technology Museum in Pudong has hands-on exhibits and a robotics lab, with adult tickets around CNY 45.
The Shanghai Jewish Refugees Museum in the former Ohel Moshe Synagogue covers the WWII-era Hongkou refugee sector with documents, photographs and a memorial wall.
Power Station of Art, China's state-run contemporary art museum in a former power plant on the Huangpu riverside, hosts the Shanghai Biennale and free-to-enter exhibitions.
Longhua Temple, the city's largest Buddhist temple, is open to visitors for a small fee and holds an annual temple fair and a New Year's Eve bell-striking ceremony.
LINK Parkour runs parkour training at SOHOGYM on Yongtai Lu in Xuhui and a second site on Pingji Lu.

Party King Bowling Sports Bar in the Dimei Shopping Center off Renmin Avenue near People's Square hosts group game nights with bowling, archery, foosball and billiards for about RMB 150 including a drink.
venue: Party King Bowling Sports Bar (Dimei Shopping Center)

how: Party King Bowling Sports Bar offers archery as part of its unlimited-play game nights, and the ASAS Archery Battle community runs weekend archery-tag games organised through WeChat.
venue: Party King Bowling Sports Bar (Dimei Shopping Center)

how: RunnersHai holds free social runs and coached training on the West Bund on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and weekend mornings, and the Shanghai Hash House Harriers run a new route every Sunday afternoon.

Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel) runs a Sunday afternoon heritage walk, 'Secrets, Spies & Art Deco', through the former French Concession from Jiangsu Road to Huashan Road, and Weekend Riverfront City Walk leads bilingual walks along the Bund, Suzhou Creek and the former French Concession.
venue: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel)

how: Shanghai FUN is a bilingual social community with over 8,000 members and a 1,000-event history, running regular social nights, networking and classes at venues around Jing'an and the Bund.

Shanghai Sahaja Yoga Meditation offers free guided meditation sessions with no prior experience needed, listed as online Zoom sessions; in person, the Learn Qigong in Shanghai group teaches gentle qigong in English at Fuxing Park.
venue: Learn Qigong in Shanghai (Fuxing Park) / Shanghai Sahaja Yoga Meditation

how: The Second Languages & Cross Culture's Communication meetup group hosts a Saturday evening board games night in the roadshow hall of Fudan Science Park.
venue: Fudan Science Park (Saturday Shanghai Board Games)

activity: Hands-on cooking classes (pasta and other cuisines)
how: OKDeal Travel / Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai host 'Authentic China Tastes' cooking classes, including one with a Michelin chef in the Jing'an Temple area.
venue: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel)

how: Dramamoves.com Projects, a bespoke wine service behind Plaza 66, runs drop-in tastings of French and Italian wines from independent producers; no WSET course was confirmed.
XinCheJian, China's first hackerspace (2010), is a volunteer-run nonprofit in Huangpu with monthly memberships, Wednesday open nights and electronics workshops.
XinCheJian runs workshops on Arduino, PCB design and robot building (e.g. Otto robot, DIY drone).
XinCheJian hackerspace provides 3D printing among its member facilities.
XinCheJian hackerspace provides laser cutting among its member facilities.
XinCheJian hackerspace lists machine work and digital fabrication among its member facilities; CNC specifically was not confirmed.
Shanghai Library runs a regular public lecture series (Shanghai Library Lectures) alongside exhibitions and training courses at its Huaihai Road and East branches.
Shanghai Library holds historical literature collections and a Genealogy Library open to readers at its Huaihai Road branch.
Shanghai is flat delta land with no natural crags; local gyms such as Roaring Climbing Gym in Hongkou organise outdoor climbing trips out of the city.
Shanghai's mild climate gives little reliable snow; large snow sculpture exhibitions are held in Harbin each winter, roughly a 3-hour flight away.
Shanghai has several Toastmasters clubs listed in the club directory, including Shanghai People's Square Toastmasters Club, Shanghai Xujiahui Toastmasters Club and Shanghai No.1 Toastmasters Club.
Dragonfly (悠庭) is a chain of massage and beauty spas with branches in Shanghai offering classic massage for men and women with online booking.
The Shanghai Jewish Refugees Museum in the former Ohel Moshe Synagogue preserves the heritage of the Jewish community that sheltered in Hongkou in the 1930s and 1940s.
A self-guided half-day walk through the former French Concession starting at Wukang Road and Huaihai Road is recommended by the city tourism guide, and Hongkou's 1933 Old Millfun is free to enter.
Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel) lists xiaolongbao and dumpling-making cooking classes among its hands-on cultural activities.
venue: Urban Fun Experiences in Shanghai (OKDeal Travel)
